image.alt: Illustrated map of central Berlin Mitte showing the BerlinWalk tour route from Alexanderplatz to Hackescher Markt

stops.name: World Clock
stops.hook: Where the walk begins. A Cold War-era monument under which generations of Berliners have met without giving an address.

stops.name: TV Tower
stops.hook: East Berlin's tallest statement. Built in 1969 to outshine the West, with a reflective cross the Pope's Revenge story explains.

stops.name: Rotes Rathaus & Neptunbrunnen
stops.hook: Red brick that has watched Berlin become Berlin since 1869: empire, war, division, reunification, all from one balcony. In front, four river goddesses sit around a sea god most people never stop to look at.

stops.name: St. Mary's Church
stops.hook: Berlin's second oldest church, with a medieval dance-of-death fresco inside that survived everything the 20th century threw at it.

stops.name: Marx-Engels Forum
stops.hook: Two seated philosophers, a bit weathered. The plaza around them tells a longer story than the statue itself.

stops.name: Sanchi Gate
stops.hook: A copy of a stone gateway from the Great Stupa at Sanchi in India, standing beside a rebuilt Prussian palace. It asks whose history a museum city chooses to show.

stops.name: Humboldt Forum
stops.hook: Demolished, then rebuilt as a near-replica 60 years later. The most controversial reconstruction in modern Berlin.

stops.name: Lustgarten, Berliner Dom & Altes Museum
stops.hook: Royal garden, parade ground, rally site and a garden again, framed by the cathedral's green dome and Berlin's first public museum from 1830.

stops.name: Neues Museum, Alte Nationalgalerie & Pergamon
stops.hook: Nefertiti's home, a temple of 19th-century German painting and the Pergamon Museum behind its renovation fences. UNESCO-protected and hard-won.

stops.name: Friedrichsbrücke
stops.hook: The bridge off Museum Island. Stop halfway and look back at the cathedral and the museums before the last stretch.

stops.name: Hackescher Markt
stops.hook: Where the walk ends and Berlin's courtyards begin. Coffee, the S-Bahn and the rest of your day.
